hypothesis: Two records of the same past event, carried by gravitational waves and by light, travel at the same speed. Layer 1: the parent action propagates tensor waves at c (c_T = 1, derived in test_tensor_speed.py). Observation layer, principle P1: each carrier delivers the source state at its own retarded time, so the arrival delay of the two records equals their emission delay only. Predicted (v_GW - v_EM)/v_EM = 0 exactly.

observable.domain: binary neutron star merger GW170817 and GRB 170817A, about 40 Mpc

prediction_method.description: prediction 0 from c_T = 1 of the parent action; PASS if 0 lies inside the published interval [-3e-15, +7e-16]

fixed_parameters: c_T = 1 from the parent action (no X-dependent coupling)
pass_criterion: PASS if 0 lies inside the published interval of (v_GW - v_EM)/v_EM.
fail_criterion: FAILED if 0 lies outside the interval; INCONCLUSIVE if the registered values disagree with the source text.
note: Disclosure: drafted after reading the published bound, and any theory with c_T = 1 passes, so the outcome is effectively known. The parent action has no term that could change c_T, so this test checks the structure rather than a free parameter; it would fail only if the action were changed to couple R to derivatives of the scalar. It confronts principle P1 (records of one event via two carriers) and layer 1 together. Approved by the author on 2026-11-11 as drafted.
